relationships.subject: PGE2
relationships.evidence_quote: Endogenous PGE<sub>2</sub> increased the spontaneous but not the distention-induced release of s-NTD via EP2 and EP3 prostanoid receptors

relationships.subject: EP2 receptor
relationships.evidence_quote: suggesting that endogenous PGE2 stimulated release of s-NTDs by activating EP2 and EP3 receptors on cells in the LP

relationships.subject: soluble nucleotidases
relationships.evidence_quote: Once released, ATP is degraded sequentially to ADP, AMP, and ADO by a large number of membrane-bound and soluble/releasable NTDs

key_findings: Endogenous PGE2 increases spontaneous (not distention-induced) soluble nucleotidase release in bladder LP via EP2 and EP3; exogenous PGE2 acts via EP3/EP4/FP.
Higher PG levels may potentiate ATP degradation as a safeguard against bladder overactivity.
